title: U.S. House · California's 40th District
area: Western Riverside County and eastern Orange County, including Corona, Norco, and parts of La Habra and Yorba Linda.

context.text: This is a battleground race between two sitting Republican incumbents. Redistricting under Proposition 50, approved by voters in November 2025, drew Rep. Ken Calvert (previously representing the 41st District) and Rep. Young Kim (previously representing the 40th District) into the same new 40th District. Calvert represents an estimated 51% of the new district's population and Kim about 35%. Both advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which Calvert received 35% of the vote and Kim 21%, defeating six other candidates; no Democrat advanced.

Both campaigns have run negative advertisements. As of July 9, 2026, Calvert had been endorsed by gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton, the California Republican Assembly, and the California Congress of Republicans; Kim had been endorsed by U.S. Rep. James Gallagher, state Senate Minority Leader Brian Jones, and Americans for Prosperity Action.

candidates.name: Ken Calvert
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, previously for California's 41st District (since 1993)

summary.text: Ken Calvert is a Republican who has represented Riverside County in the U.S. House since 1992 after a career as a restaurant and real-estate small-business owner. He chairs the Defense subcommittee of the House Appropriations Committee, and Proposition 50 redistricting placed him in the same new 40th District as fellow Republican incumbent Young Kim. In the June 2 top-two primary he received 35% of the vote to Kim's 21%.

background.text: Born in Corona, California, on June 8, 1953, and describes himself as a lifelong resident of Riverside County; graduated from Corona High School in 1971.
Attended Chaffey College (an associate degree in 1973, per Ballotpedia) and graduated from San Diego State University in 1975 with a bachelor's degree in economics.

As a teenager he joined the 1970 congressional campaign of former state Assemblyman Victor Veysey and later interned in Veysey's Washington, D.C., office after Veysey's 1972 re-election, according to Wikipedia.

According to his official biography, he was a 17-year small-business owner in the restaurant and real estate industries; Ballotpedia lists restaurant manager among his past jobs. He also chaired the Riverside County Republican Party.
According to his official biography, he has held leadership roles with local volunteer organizations including the Corona Chamber of Commerce, the Corona Rotary and the Corona-Norco Family YMCA.

Lost the 1982 Republican primary for a newly drawn House seat to Riverside County Supervisor Al McCandless, then won a new district in 1992, defeating Democrat Mark Takano by 519 votes with 47% of the vote, according to Wikipedia.
First elected to the U.S. House in 1992; his official biography describes him as one of the chamber's most senior members and the dean of the California Republican delegation.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Defense Subcommittee and sits on the Energy and Water Development Subcommittee in the 119th Congress; Ballotpedia lists him as Defense subcommittee chair for 2023 onward.

After Proposition 50 redrew California's congressional districts in 2025, he was drawn into the 40th District with Young Kim; the two Republican incumbents advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, with Calvert receiving 35% and Kim 21%.

priorities.text: Campaigning on his legislative record, citing top ratings from Americans for Tax Reform, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, the National Federation of Independent Businesses, the National Association of Manufacturers, and the 60 Plus Association, and highlighting his legislation creating the E-Verify employment-verification system and federal funding for transportation and environmental projects.
priorities.quote: Ken's legislative work has received top ratings from the Americans for Tax Reform, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, National Federation of Independent Businesses, National Association of Manufacturers, and the 60 Plus Association.

positions.summary: Voted for the Laken Riley Act requiring DHS to detain undocumented immigrants charged with or convicted of theft and other offenses, and said he voted for it to protect Americans from those who do not abide by the law.
positions.quote: I voted for the Laken Riley Act to protect Americans from violent criminals and those who have demonstrated time and time again that they cannot abide by our laws.

record.text: Chairs the Defense Subcommittee of the House Committee on Appropriations and also serves on its Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies subcommittee in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).
Authored legislation creating the E-Verify system used to check employees' legal work status, according to his campaign.

candidates.name: Young Kim
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, previously for California's 40th District (since 2021)

summary.text: Young Kim is a Republican who was born in Incheon, South Korea, worked as a financial analyst and as a longtime aide to Rep. Ed Royce, and served in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016. She has been in the U.S. House since January 2021 and serves on the Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees, where she chairs the East Asia and the Pacific Subcommittee. Redistricting placed her in the same new 40th District as fellow Republican incumbent Ken Calvert, and she is running on her record in Congress.

background.text: Born in Incheon, South Korea, in 1962 and raised in Seoul; her family left South Korea in 1975, living first in Guam and then Hawaii, according to Wikipedia. Her official biography describes her as an immigrant.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Southern California in 1985.

Worked as a financial analyst at First Interstate Bank and as a controller at JK Sportswear Manufacturing, and started her own clothing-industry business, according to Wikipedia; her official biography calls her a small business owner.

Worked for Ed Royce, first in his state Senate office and then for 21 years in his congressional office as community liaison and director of Asian affairs, according to Wikipedia; Ballotpedia lists her as his director of community relations and Asian affairs.
Represented District 65 in the California State Assembly from 2014 to 2016, winning in 2014 over Democratic incumbent Sharon Quirk-Silva and losing to Quirk-Silva in 2016.

Ran for the open California 39th Congressional District in 2018 and lost to Democrat Gil Cisneros, 51.6% to 48.4%; won the 2020 rematch and was sworn in on January 3, 2021, as one of the first Korean American women in Congress.

Ran for re-election in the 40th District after the 2021 redistricting and won again in 2024; in the 119th Congress she serves on the Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees, chairs the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, and serves on the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.
According to her official biography, she and her husband Charles live in Anaheim Hills and have four children and two grandchildren; Ballotpedia lists her residence as La Habra.

priorities.text: Campaigning on her record in Congress supporting President Trump's agenda and says she is working to reverse Biden-era policy on prices, crime, and border security.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I continue to fight every day to ensure President Trump has allies to undo the disastrous Joe Biden-Nancy Pelosi agenda that caused skyrocketing prices, rising crime, an open border, and a political class that serves the swamp instead of fighting for working families.

positions.summary: Introduced the REPORT Act requiring the President to notify Congress and justify tariff changes; said tariffs can be a strategic tool but that long-term tariffs can raise prices for families and small businesses.
positions.quote: While tariffs can be an important strategic tool to help level the playing field between the United States and other countries, long-term tariffs can be a tax that hike prices and hurt the bottom line for American families and small businesses

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, where she chairs the Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, and on the House Committee on Financial Services and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.
